skill.name: data-engineering-data-pipeline
skill.description: Guides data pipeline architecture for batch, streaming, orchestration, storage, quality, monitoring, and cost optimization.
skill.summary: Design reliable batch and streaming data pipelines with practical architecture guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives in the reviewed SKILL.md context. The flagged locations are data engineering prose or a Python example block, with no shell execution, system probing, network scanning, or prompt injection intent found.

remediation.issue: Example code uses real-looking PostgreSQL and S3 placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Label sample connection strings and storage paths as placeholders to reduce confusion during implementation.

static_findings.snippet: - Schema validation and dead letter queue for invalid records
- Alerts: failures, performance degradation, data freshness

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 122-157 are a fenced Python example for batch ingestion and Delta Lake writes. No shell backticks, subprocess calls, or external command execution are present.
Line 47 describes schema validation and a dead letter queue for invalid data records. It does not request host inspection, credential discovery, or system reconnaissance.
Line 114 gives storage partitioning guidance for data lake file layout. It contains no instruction to enumerate local systems or collect environment details.
Lines 182-183 discuss operational alerts and dashboards for pipeline health. They do not describe scanning networks, discovering services, or contacting unknown endpoints.

content.value_statement: Data pipeline projects often fail from unclear architecture, weak quality checks, and poor operational planning. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structure reliable batch and streaming pipelines.
actual_capabilities: Compares ETL, ELT, Lambda, Kappa, and Lakehouse pipeline patterns.
Outlines batch and streaming ingestion practices, including retries and replay.
Guides orchestration with Airflow and Prefect concepts.
Covers dbt, Spark, Delta Lake, and Iceberg design choices.
Defines monitoring, alerting, quality checks, and cost optimization considerations.
limitations: Does not provide runnable source files or installable pipeline components.
Requires users to adapt examples to their cloud, warehouse, and security controls.
Does not validate live infrastructure, credentials, schemas, or production costs.
May need specialist review for regulated data or strict compliance environments.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Analytics Pipeline
use_cases.description: Create a practical architecture for ingesting operational data into a warehouse or lakehouse.

use_cases.title: Review Pipeline Reliability
use_cases.description: Check a proposed pipeline for retries, dead letter handling, monitoring, and data quality coverage.

use_cases.title: Control Pipeline Costs
use_cases.description: Identify partitioning, file sizing, lifecycle, and compute choices that can reduce infrastructure spend.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pipeline Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between ETL, ELT, Lambda, Kappa, and Lakehouse for this data pipeline. Ask for missing requirements first.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Ingestion Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Design batch and streaming ingestion for these sources, volumes, latency targets, and failure handling needs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Quality and Observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pipeline design for data quality, monitoring, alerting, replay, and operational risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Lakehouse Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this lakehouse pipeline for partitioning, file sizing, compaction, storage lifecycle, and compute cost improvements.

output_examples.input: Design a daily orders pipeline from PostgreSQL to a lakehouse.
output: Recommended pattern: ELT with incremental batch extraction.
Key components: source watermarking, schema validation, Delta Lake storage, dbt marts, and freshness alerts.
Operational notes: add retries, a dead letter queue, and daily quality reports.

output_examples.input: Review my Kafka pipeline for reliability gaps.
output: Add transactional offset commits to reduce duplicate processing risk.
Define replay procedures for failed events and late data.
Track failed records, lag, throughput, and freshness in dashboards.

best_practices: Start with source volume, latency, data quality, and target serving requirements.
Design retry, replay, and dead letter handling before production release.
Track freshness, failures, quality scores, cost, and throughput from launch.
anti_patterns: Do not choose streaming when batch latency already meets the business need.
Do not over-partition lake storage into many small files.
Do not ship pipelines without ownership, alert routing, and rollback procedures.

faq.question: Can this skill generate production pipeline code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation structure and examples, but users must adapt and test all code for their environment.

faq.question: Does it support both batch and streaming pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers batch ingestion, streaming ingestion, orchestration, storage, quality checks, and monitoring.

faq.question: Which orchestration tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for Airflow and Prefect concepts such as task grouping, retries, caching, and visibility.

faq.question: Can it help with data quality design?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers schema validation, Great Expectations, dbt tests, freshness checks, and failure notifications.

faq.question: Does it connect to cloud services directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples, but it does not run commands or connect to external services.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Data engineers, platform engineers, analytics engineers, and technical leads planning or reviewing data pipelines can use it.
